title: AI Modeling for HIV Antibody Research
kicker: Graduate Course Project · Protein Language Models
tools: Protein Models (ESM3, LoRA, VAE) · Machine Learning (XGBoost, scikit-learn)
blurb: Predicting HIV antibody breadth from sequence: frozen ESM3 embeddings raised AUROC from 0.651 to 0.773 on 300 antibodies, though the interval includes zero.
long: Broadly neutralizing antibodies block many HIV strains at once, and finding them is slow lab work. This project asked how much a sequence-only model can say about breadth before any physical assay.

On 300 public heavy-chain sequences from CATNAP, grouped into 109 lineages so that relatives never sit on both sides of a split, frozen ESM3 embeddings reached a pooled AUROC of 0.773 against 0.651 for the handcrafted XGBoost baseline. The group-bootstrap interval of the difference still includes zero, and the write-up says so.

Adapted ESM3 with LoRA on OAS antibody repertoires for the lineage case studies. That adaptation run did not improve downstream performance, but in its representation space it placed 4 of 4 known VRC34 intermediates correctly.
Reconciled every number in the report against the saved artifacts with an audit script, so the claims and the results cannot drift apart.
